classification.difficultyReason: The parts are heavily scaffolded using the denominator-9 pattern. Part a gives 9/9 and part b simplifies it, so the student must interpret that 0.9 recurring equals 1. Part c uses 'hence' to shift one place (divide by 10). Part d, the hardest, needs the student to split 0.4 recurring 9 into 0.4 + 0.0 recurring 9 and add fractions. This is a linked procedure with some conceptual interpretation, above the guided algebraic conversions of p5-q7. It is comparable to, or slightly easier than, p5-q6, which mixes several recurring-decimal forms with no scaffold.
